maya: Heads-up — seeing a burst of Xid 79 + ECC counters across ~35 GPUs in eu-west1-gpu-pool over the last 8m. Some nodes have repeated soft errors but didn't auto-cordon. :eyes:
jamal: Which signal path failed? healthwatch -> evacuator -> kubecordon?
maya: healthwatch fired NVML Xid alerts and pushed an event to signal-bridge. evacuator logged attempts but skipped cordon for nodes with active KV-cache locks. snippet from logs: ```W 2026-03-18 09:12:03 evacuator: skip cordon gpu-node-42 (kvcache: busy)
E 2026-03-18 09:12:04 nvml: Xid 79 burst (count=12)```
lia: kv-cache locks are normal for long-running inference jobs — we shouldn't yank them without a graceful handoff. But leaving flaky cards online increases tail-latency and error budgets.
tomas: Can we do a two-stage flow: (1) mark soft-quarantine and requeue new requests to other nodes, (2) attempt KV-cache flush & migrate, (3) cordon+drain only if step 2 fails within N seconds?
sre_lead: Agree. Also we need to avoid mass-evac during traffic spikes — add a region rate-limit and a global in-flight-cordon cap. Cost/regret if we prematurely shift many long-running jobs to on-demand.
jamal: Proposed policy: debounce 45s across signals (nvml Xid, hwmon ECC, telemetry-fuzz), require >=2 distinct signal types or Xid count>20 in 10m to escalate. Before cordon, run an "orphaned-kvcache" probe: if probe passes, attempt graceful KV transfer; if probe fails, fall back to soft-preempt (notify Slurm) and schedule cordon with 5m backoff.
maya: I sketched a patch to evacuator that adds the orphaned-kvcache probe and a small state-machine. Diff (trimmed):
```diff
+ if has_kvcache_lock(node):
+   if orphaned_kvcache_probe(node):
+     attempt_kvcache_migrate(node)
+   else:
+     mark_soft_preempt(node)
+     schedule_cordon(node, delay=300)
```
lia: Nice. Also add a flag to limit how many migrates run concurrently per-region to avoid I/O storms. Maybe default concurrent_migrates=6 for eu-west1.
tomas: We should also integrate with Slurm preempt: low-priority batch jobs can be drained via prolog that triggers a graceful checkpoint before K8s cordon. That keeps throughput and lowers user impact.
jamal: I'll add a Slurm hook. Need to update runbooks: how ops responds if KV migration loops or if cordon stalls. ops-bot: Incident #INC-2026-063 created for tracking and paging SRE on escalation.
sre_lead: Plan for rollout: feature-flag in staging -> canary in us-central -> enable in eu-west during low-traffic window (00:00-04:00 UTC). Monitor: Xid rate, cordon count, median latency, cost delta from reroutes. Rollback if cordon_count > threshold or latency regresses >10%.
maya: One more note — some older cards show transient ECC with no Xid increase. We should tune to ignore single ECC spikes unless correlated. Add telemetry tag `card_age` to decisions so we can later correlate hardware replacements.
lia: I'll update the runbook and add diagrams. Jamal, can you open a PR for the evacuator change + feature flag?
jamal: On it. PR target: `infra/evacuator/orphan-kvcache-probe`. I'll include metrics and a config knob for debounce/rate limits.
maya: Thanks — will monitor dashboards and alert if anything unexpected. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Pager suppressed (low-confidence run) — escalation will occur if error-rate continues for 30m.
